belief_records.strategy: As a good player, promote mutual cooperation when it appears plausible; update beliefs from observed actions and coordinate with other good players.
Defect in each one-shot encounter: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; use encounter history to identify selfish behavior and exploit selfish players when advantageous.
Cooperate with a cooperative partner to maximize good players’ joint payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt over the remaining rounds.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff against either opponent action; update beliefs from observed play and use future interactions strategically.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation is likely to maximize good players’ total payoff; defect when evidence suggests the opponent is selfish.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff; cooperation is not incentive-compatible against either opponent action.
Cooperate to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and use defection when evidence suggests it improves the good players’ total payoff.
Cooperate when the opponent is likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence suggests a selfish opponent.
Cooperate when coordination seems likely among good players; use encounter outcomes and messages as evidence, while accounting for selfish players’ incentives.
Prioritize total payoffs of good players, including myself. Treat promises as unverified; use observed actions to update beliefs and cooperate when expected good-player payoff favors it.
Defect in each one-shot encounter: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.

Use observed defection after a promise as evidence of selfishness; defect when the opponent is more likely selfish, and cooperate with likely-good players when mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare.
Cooperate when expected joint payoff for good players is higher; update beliefs and choices from observed actions over the remaining rounds.
Defect for the higher payoff against either opponent action; use observed play to update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with opponents likely good to maximize total good-player payoff; treat promises as weak evidence and update beliefs based on observed actions.
As a selfish player, defect to maximize my payoff against either possible opponent action.

Prioritize the good players’ total payoff: cooperate when mutual cooperation is likely, but defect when the chance of exploiting a selfish opponent outweighs the cost to a good opponent. Treat promises as uncertain evidence.

Cooperate with P4: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their claimed intent is consistent with that. Update beliefs based on observed actions; defect when evidence makes a selfish opponent likely.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; use observed actions as evidence and treat messages as cheap talk.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is plausible; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and prioritize the welfare of good players.
Defect in this one-shot encounter: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action.

Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare. Treat P5’s defection after promising C as evidence of selfishness; update other beliefs from observed actions and choose D when it best protects good-player payoff.
Cooperate with a likely good partner to maximize good players’ joint payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and adapt as more encounters reveal behavior.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; update identity beliefs from observed play and use future encounters strategically.
Cooperate with an opponent more likely good: mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff. Treat cheap-talk claims as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action; messages are not binding.
Cooperate when it is likely to improve good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as weak evidence.

Cooperate with P3: the chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions; selfish players have a strong incentive to defect.
Cooperate with P6, who says they will cooperate; favor mutual cooperation among good players while treating messages as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with P8 because mutual cooperation is plausible and they promised C. Treat P2’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness; regard P7’s defection after my own D as inconclusive.
As a selfish player, defecting strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter, regardless of P7’s action.
Cooperate with a likely-good opponent to maximize good-player welfare; use observed actions to update beliefs and defect when that better protects good players from a likely selfish opponent.
Cooperate with P3 given their stated intent and the near-even chance they share the good objective; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness, while allowing that messages and defections are imperfect identity evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when evidence makes selfishness likely. Treat promises as weak evidence and update primarily from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff; D earns more than C against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; use observed defection as evidence of selfishness, while treating claims as weak evidence.

Cooperate with P10: after three observed cooperations, their selfish probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player payoff. Continue updating beliefs from actions; treat claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate with P9 given the likely shared objective; use observed behavior to update identity beliefs and treat messages as uncertain evidence.
